plan:
Identify a suitable 7-inch 6S quadcopter frame kit to support the 1.5kg takeoff weight and specified components.
Integrate Holybro Pixhawk 6C Mini flight controller, Holybro M10 GPS, Holybro PM07 Power Module, and Benewake TFmini Plus for flight control and basic sensing.
Mount Raspberry Pi 5 and Luxonis OAK-D S2, ensuring proper vibration isolation and power supply via Matek BEC12S-PRO.
Select appropriate motors and ESCs to achieve a thrust-to-weight ratio of approximately 2 with GNB 6S batteries.
Design and 3D print custom mounts/enclosures for the Raspberry Pi 5, OAK-D S2, TFmini Plus, and analog FPV system.
Implement both analog FPV for remote control and develop ROS/MAVLink interface for Raspberry Pi 5 autonomous control and target tracking.

research.summary: This 7-inch 1400kV brushless motor is an electrical actuator designed for high-performance drone applications, typically paired with 7-inch propellers. Its 1400kV rating indicates approximately 1400 RPM per volt, offering significant power output suitable for the front-left rotor position of a 7-inch drone. It operates efficiently on 4-6S LiPo batteries, providing strong thrust for agile flight characteristics.

originalPrompt: 我想要搭建一款7寸6S的通用四旋翼，起飞重量约1.5kg，推重比在2左右，飞控选用Holybro Pixhawk 6C Mini，并且能够搭载一台树莓派5以及OAK-D S2双目深度相机，通过双目相机及简单前向测距模块作为输入，结合飞行姿态参数，由树莓派5给出目标跟踪的输出指令。四旋翼能够实现基于模拟信号摄像头及图传系统的遥控飞行，也可以实现由树莓派5控制的自主飞行。相关的硬件推荐使用如下：电池：GNB 6S电池；飞控：Holybro Pixhawk 6C Mini；伴飞计算机：Raspberry Pi 5；飞控电源模块：Holybro PM07 Power Module；深度视觉主相机：Luxonis OAK-D S2；GPS/罗盘：Holybro M10 GPS；简单前向测距模块：Benewake TFmini Plus；树莓派独立供电：Matek BEC12S-PRO

subSteps.title: 3D print the Raspberry Pi 5 Vibration Isolated Mount
3D print the OAK-D S2 Camera Mount
3D print the TFmini Plus Front Sensor Mount
3D print the GPS Mast Mount
3D print the Analog FPV Camera Mount (TPU)
Test fit all 3D printed parts with their respective electrical components
Solder ESC power wires to the Power Module and motor wires to ESCs
Solder main battery connector to the Power Module, RPi5 BEC, and OAK-D S2 BEC inputs
Connect Power Module to Flight Controller power input and ESC signal wires to FC PWM outputs
Connect GPS/Compass module to Flight Controller UART and I2C ports
Connect Forward Range Sensor to Flight Controller UART
Connect RC Receiver to Flight Controller UART
Connect RPi5 BEC to Companion Computer power and OAK-D S2 BEC to Depth Camera power
Connect Analog FPV Camera to Video Transmitter and both to Power Module for power
Flash Flight Controller firmware (e.g., ArduPilot/PX4) and perform initial setup
Verify GPS and Compass sensor recognition and calibration within FC software
Verify Forward Range Sensor recognition and functionality with Flight Controller
Configure RC Receiver with Flight Controller and calibrate radio sticks
Install Raspberry Pi OS on Companion Computer and update software packages
Test OAK-D S2 Depth Camera connection to Companion Computer via USB 3.0
Confirm Analog FPV Camera and Video Transmitter operation with FPV goggles (not in BOM)
Assemble the 7-inch Dead Cat Frame Kit using M3 screws and standoffs
Mount the Flight Controller and Power Module to the frame using M3 nylon standoffs
Mount the Raspberry Pi 5 Vibration Isolated Mount to the frame and secure the Companion Computer
Attach the OAK-D S2 Camera Mount to the frame (or RPi5 mount) and secure the Depth Camera
Mount the TFmini Plus Front Sensor Mount to the front of the frame and secure the Forward Range Sensor
Attach the GPS Mast Mount to the top plate and secure the GPS/Compass module
Mount the Analog FPV Camera using its mount to the front of the frame and position the Video Transmitter
Secure the Main Battery to the frame using the Lipo Battery Pad and Strap, and perform final cable routing

projectDescription: This 7-inch quadcopter, with a 1.5kg takeoff weight and ~2 thrust-to-weight ratio, achieves autonomous flight and target tracking using a Raspberry Pi 5 companion computer and an OAK-D S2 depth camera. It integrates a flight controller for stable control and analog FPV for real-time video transmission.

assumptions: Basic soldering experience is assumed for electrical connections.
Familiarity with assembling FPV drone frames and components.
Basic understanding of Raspberry Pi OS setup and configuration.
